methodological_rigor.justification: Rigorous preclinical studies across multiple murine PDAC models (CKP, KPC, KPCY, FKPC2GP) with clear experimental design. GATA6 functional validation using CRISPR-Cas9 knockout with nontargeting controls and auxin-inducible degron system for temporal protein degradation. Spatial analysis with Phenocycler multiplex imaging on human tissues (n=8, 143 patient TMA). Multiple independent approaches confirm GATA6 causality. Statistics: unpaired Mann-Whitney, One-way ANOVA, Wilcoxon tests with replication numbers documented. Flow cytometry, RNA-seq, IHC, co-culture assays all clearly methodologically described.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical study (LoE: 5) combining murine tumor models and primary human tumor tissue analysis without clinical trial data. Mechanistic insight: demonstrates GATA6 regulates MEKi-induced MHCI upregulation; combined MEKi+HDACi enhances GATA6+ populations and immune infiltration in murine models. Translational relevance moderate: identifies therapeutic strategy with potential clinical application but proof-of-concept limited to in vitro and murine systems. No patient outcomes or clinical validation provided; gap between preclinical findings and human efficacy remains unaddressed.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive ARRIVE adherence for preclinical animal research. Detailed methods: animal ethics approvals with specific German institutional license numbers; murine strains with genotype specifications; treatment protocols with drug doses/schedules; imaging and molecular methods. RNA-seq data available in GEO (GSE146348). Public datasets explicitly cited (GSE93326, GSE212966). Human cohort ethics documented with approval numbers. Experimental replicates clearly noted (n values provided per experiment). Supplementary datasets referenced extensively. High transparency enabling reproducibility.

novelty_literature.justification: Novel mechanistic contribution: identifies GATA6 as essential regulator of MEKi-induced MHCI upregulation in PDAC; establishes causality via CRISPR knockout and AID degradation system. Combined MEKi+HDACi strategy to preserve GATA6+ populations and enhance immune infiltration addresses adaptive resistance mechanism. Demonstrates tumor cell phenotype-immune interaction dynamics during therapy. GATA6-MHCI-CD8 T cell axis characterized in spatial and single-cell transcriptomic context. Fills gap in understanding how tumor cell state transitions influence checkpoint inhibitor efficacy in PDAC.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured progression from human cohort analysis (Figure 1) to murine mechanistic studies (Figure 2+). Methods exceptionally detailed: explicit animal ethics, genotypes, treatment schedules, imaging protocols. Results systematic: GATA6 expression correlates with immune infiltration in humans; MEKi induces GATA6-dependent MHCI in cell lines; GATA6 degradation ablates effect; in vivo combination therapy shows benefit. Figures effectively communicate findings. Supplementary materials extensive. Discussion contextualizes within PDAC immunotherapy resistance literature. Minor: dense methods but appropriately comprehensive for reproducibility.

key_strengths: Novel mechanistic insight: establishes GATA6 as essential regulator of MEKi-induced MHCI upregulation via rigorous CRISPR knockout and auxin-inducible degron system confirming causality

Multimodal human validation: tissue microarray (n=143) and spatial Phenocycler analysis (n=8) confirm GATA6+ cells express higher MHCI and interact with CD8+ T cells; single-cell and bulk RNA-seq support findings

Innovative therapeutic strategy: combined MEKi+HDACi preserves GATA6+ tumor populations, enhances MHCI and CD8+ T cell infiltration in orthotopic/PDX murine models, addressing adaptive resistance mechanism
Rigorous preclinical design: comprehensive ethics approvals, multiple murine models, clear treatment protocols, T cell cytotoxicity assays with quantified GzmB/TNFa production
key_concerns: Limited clinical translation: preclinical only (LoE 5); no patient outcome data or clinical trial validation that MEKi+HDACi combination translates efficacy from murine models to human PDAC treatment

Human tissue analysis correlative only: spatial imaging on 8 PDAC cases and TMA IHC on 143 patients shows associations between GATA6 and immune infiltration but not causality or therapeutic response prediction
Murine model generalizability: CKP/KPC models may not fully recapitulate human PDAC heterogeneity; GATA6-dependent responses require validation in human organoids or patient-derived systems

Incomplete mechanistic characterization: identifies GATA6 regulates MHCI upon MEKi but does not fully elucidate downstream transcriptional targets or define molecular mechanisms enabling HDAC inhibitor protection of GATA6+ cells
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 3 paper: rigorous preclinical mechanistic study with multimodal validation identifying GATA6-dependent pathway for MEKi-induced MHCI and proposing MEKi+HDACi combination. Appropriate for Tier 3 given strong preclinical evidence but lack of clinical validation. Minor revisions recommended regarding human sample characterization and clinical translation pathway.
